curated.instructions: omr/instructions/854-1/ (scans; the go-kart is pages 1-8, alternate models after)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column, held at an angle on a frame of rods, turns through a universal joint an axle whose 8-tooth gear slides the rack on the tie rod between the two wheel turntables.
functions.source: book: steps 3-10 (rods in steps 4-6, rack in step 7, universal joint and gear in step 9, wheel in step 10)

functions.does: The rear wheels work the engine as the kart rolls: the 24-tooth gear on the right rear axle drives an 8-tooth gear on a short axle, and two 24-tooth gears face to face with an axle 4 through their outer holes make a crankshaft, whose connecting rod pumps the piston up and down in the engine block behind the seat.
functions.source: book: step 3 and its inset (the crankshaft), steps 5 and 10-11 (the piston and engine block)

functions.does: The nose with the number board hangs on the axle across the very front.
functions.source: book: steps 4-5 and 8; inferred: unsure whether the nose is meant to stay put or to tip on its axle
functions.note: Kinebrick today lets the nose (p50 and the parts on it) swing freely on the front axle p24.

questions.question: Should the number board on the nose stay put?

854-Go Kart: 0 // Kinebrick: its front wheels turn alike, so at full lock, about 33 degrees, where a knuckle meets its chassis, its tyres scrub sideways by up to 16% of how far they roll
